one_liner: Agentic B2B support platform for humans and AI agents to collaborate.
auth_notes: The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication with an API token generated in the Pylon dashboard. MCP uses OAuth 2.0.
access_notes: Pylon is a B2B SaaS platform requiring a paid account or contacting sales/booking a demo to get production credentials and access.
api_notes: Covers issues, organization, user details, and other support endpoints. Base URL varies by region (api.usepylon.com or api.eu.usepylon.com).
blocker_notes: Pylon requires a B2B contract/paid account as it is a commercial support tool without a public self-serve free tier.

auth.quote:
The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:
Copy
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard.

api.quote:
US region: https://api.usepylon.com
EU region: https://api.eu.usepylon.com

reasons.auth: API uses bearer token authentication via Admin‑generated API tokens as shown in the OpenAPI security scheme.
reasons.access: Documentation does not state how API tokens are obtained (free sign‑up, trial, or paid), so the access tier cannot be determined.
reasons.mcp: Docs reference a "Pylon MCP" feature, indicating an official Model Context Protocol server provided by the vendor.
reasons.verdict: Public REST API documentation exists, but the lack of clear self‑serve credential acquisition means building the integration may require additional steps such as admin token creation, leading to a build_with_friction assessment.

reasons.auth: Docs show a bearerAuth security scheme (Authorization: Bearer <token>) and mention that only admin users can create API tokens.
reasons.access: No self‑serve sign‑up is described; tokens are created by admin users, implying credentials are only available to paying customers.
reasons.mcp: Pylon MCP is referenced in the product site and developer docs as an official Model Context Protocol service.
reasons.verdict: Public API documentation and token‑based auth are available, but obtaining a token requires a paid plan, so a toolkit can be built but with friction.
